texts.li: [lowtech] A few healers of {FACTION} came down the road with dried herbs in their packs and clay pots clinking at every step. They go from village to village seeing to whatever needs seeing to, {X_nameDef}, the eldest, told {A_nameDef}, and they'd like to camp {PLACE} a few days.

[!lowtech] The traveling clinic of {FACTION} turns out to be a handful of tired medics, a folding table and a crate of supplies stenciled with somebody else's name. {X_nameDef}, who runs it, told {A_nameDef} they'll set up {PLACE} for a few days and see anyone who needs seeing.

[ws:sickness] With {SITUATION} in every village, the healers of {FACTION} go where they're sent and sleep where they can. {X_nameDef}, gray with tiredness, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might rest {PLACE} a few days, and promised to see to anyone at the colony who's ailing while they're here.

[winter] Healers of {FACTION} came in out of the cold with frost on their packs. Winter is their busiest season, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}: coughs, chilblains, falls on the ice. They'd like to camp {PLACE} and rest before the next village.

Healers of {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land with a cart of remedies and a sign that says, in three languages, that they ask no questions. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} a few days, and the colony is welcome at their table.

settled.li: The healers from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a table of remedies by the fire and a torch to work by after dark.
[lowtech] Bundles of herbs hang drying around the healers' fire {PLACE}, and the smell of them carries to the colony.
[!lowtech] The healers from {FACTION} have set out their table {PLACE}, with bottles in neat rows and a clean cloth over the instruments.
A pot of something that smells like medicine is simmering at the healers' camp {PLACE}, with a bench beside it for the sick to wait on.

joinTexts.li: "You need a healer more than the road does." {X_nameDef}, one of the healers camped {PLACE}, said it plainly, and asked whether {X_pronoun} might stay.
{X_nameDef} from the healers' camp has been seeing to the colonists' scrapes and coughs every evening, unasked. Tonight {X_nameDef} asked whether there might be a place for a healer here, for good.
In a few days {X_nameDef}, the youngest of the healers {PLACE}, has learned every colonist's name and every colonist's complaint. {X_nameDef} asks whether a healer might be wanted here for good.

farewell.li: The healers from {FACTION} packed up their remedies and went on to the next village, with a long list of the colony's coughs to ask about next time.
The healers' camp {PLACE} is gone, and the smell of drying herbs with it.
[round] The healers from {FACTION} have gone. {X_nameDef} went round the colony first, looking in on everyone they'd treated.

helpTexts.li: [heal] {X_nameDef} from the healers' camp caught {A_nameDef} on the path and saw to {A_possessive} {THING} there and then, with a poultice and a cup of something bitter. {A_nameDef} is already feeling better.

[heal,lowtech] {X_nameDef}, the eldest of the healers, sat {A_nameDef} down by the camp's fire and saw to the {THING} with herbs and a lot of muttering. {A_nameDef} came back to the colony looking much brighter.
[heal,!lowtech] {X_nameDef} from the clinic {PLACE} took one look at {A_nameDef}'s {THING}, sat {A_objective} down at the folding table, and dealt with it in twenty minutes. No charge.
[herbs] The healers {PLACE} gathered more herbs at dawn than they need, and {X_nameDef} left {COUNT} bundles of herbal medicine on the colony's side of their camp.

[herbs] {X_nameDef} came back from gathering at dawn and set out {COUNT} bundles of healroot at the edge of the healers' camp for the colony's stores, with a lecture ready on keeping them dry for whoever comes to fetch them.

li.label: Let their apprentice see {A_nameDef}
li.refuseLabel: The colony's doctor will see to it

askTexts.li: The healers' apprentice needs practice, {X_nameDef} says, and the camp's people are all disgracefully well. They've heard {A_nameDef} is unwell, and ask whether the apprentice might come and see to {A_objective}, under {X_nameDef}'s eye.
{X_nameDef} came to the gate to ask whether anyone at the colony was ill. The healers' youngest has to learn on someone, {X_nameDef} said, and they'd heard {A_nameDef} was poorly.

li.tip: Their apprentice comes to {A_nameDef}'s side with the healer watching, and does what can be done for a wound, an illness or an everyday ailment.

outcomes.li: The healers' apprentice will come to see {A_nameDef} this afternoon, with {X_nameDef} looking over {X_possessive} shoulder.
{X_nameDef} is sending the apprentice up to the colony with a bag of remedies, and will come too, to watch.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} said they understood, and the apprentice went back to rolling bandages for the next town.
The healers kept to their camp.

li.label: Buy remedies from them ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: A few doses of their herbal medicine, at their price.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} wraps five bundles of remedies in clean cloth and explains each one twice.
[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} sells the colony a box of the healers' remedies, each labeled in a tidy hand.
{X_nameDef} counts out the remedies and tells {A_nameDef} which ones taste worst, so {A_nameDef} can warn the others.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} learn at their table
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends a few hours at the healers' table. Practice in medicine.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} has gone to sit at the healers' table and learn. {X_nameDef} started with how to wash {A_possessive} hands, properly.
{X_nameDef} is showing {A_nameDef} how they set a bone with two sticks and a lot of nerve.

texts.li: A procession of {FACTION} has come singing up the road behind a carried shrine: the faithful of a dozen villages, bound for a holy place far beyond the colony. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might rest {PLACE} for a few days and keep their prayers.

[ideology] Followers of {IDEO} from {FACTION} have come up the road carrying the relics of their faith on poles. {X_nameDef}, who walks at the front, asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE}, to rest and to pray.

[ideology,sameFaith] A procession of {FACTION} has arrived singing hymns the colony knows: they keep {IDEO}, the colony's own ideoligion, and they've come out of their way to rest among their own. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE}.

[ws:faith] The faithful are out on every road for {SITUATION}, and a procession of {FACTION} has stopped by the colony on its way. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} on the way.

[lowtech] The bells and drums came over the hill first, and then the procession of {FACTION} behind them, carrying a carved figure on a litter. {X_nameDef}, their leader, asked {A_nameDef} whether the figure and its people might rest {PLACE} a few nights on their long road.

[colony:Devout] A procession of {FACTION} has come out of its way to pass the colony, which the faithful on the roads call a devout place. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might rest {PLACE} and pray a while among people who would understand it.

settled.li: The faithful from {FACTION} have set their shrine down {PLACE}, with a place cleared before it for prayer and their sleeping places in a ring around the fire.
[ideology] The followers of {IDEO} have made their camp {PLACE}. Their relics stand on a cloth near the cookpot, and someone is always keeping watch over them.
At the procession's camp {PLACE}, the shrine is set facing the sunrise, with the bells hung on a pole beside it.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the faithful camped {PLACE}, says the road has brought {X_objective} where {X_pronoun} was meant to be, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay with the colony instead of walking on.
[sameFaith] {X_nameDef} from the procession {PLACE} has found people of {X_possessive} own ideoligion here. After a night spent praying on it, {X_nameDef} asks to stay.
{X_nameDef} has carried the procession's shrine far enough, {X_pronoun} says, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might set down {X_possessive} load here, among the colony.

farewell.li: The procession from {FACTION} lifted its shrine at dawn and went on singing up the road. The colony could hear them long after they'd gone out of sight.
The faithful from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} and went on toward their holy place. {X_nameDef} said they'd pray for the colony there.
The procession from {FACTION} lifted its shrine and went, bells first. At the edge of the colony's land its leader turned and blessed the place once more, over one shoulder.

lines.li: Sing it again, from the start.

momentLines.li: [blessing] Bless the hands that work it.

helpTexts.li: [blessing,fields] {X_nameDef}, the eldest of the faithful, came to the colony's fields at dusk with a bell and blessed them, and the houses and the people with them.
[blessing,gate] {X_nameDef}, the eldest of the faithful, came to the colony's gate at dusk with a bell and blessed the colony from there: its houses, its fields and its people.
[blessing,ideology] The followers of {IDEO} came to the colony at sunset and sang a blessing over it before going back to their fire.
[blessing,sameFaith] The procession came to the colony this evening to pray for it, as people of one ideoligion. {X_nameDef} led the prayers.
[blessing,lowtech,fields] The faithful went out into the colony's fields at dusk, ringing bells, so the land would be kind to the people working it.

li.label: Let them carry their icon round the fields

askTexts.li: The procession would like to carry their icon round the colony's fields before they go on, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}. It brings a good harvest, they believe, and does no harm if it doesn't.
[ideology] The faithful of {IDEO} bless the fields of every place that shelters them. {X_nameDef} came to ask leave to walk the colony's fields this morning, singing.

li.tip: The procession walks the colony's fields with their icon and their hymns for an hour or so, and whoever likes walks with them.

outcomes.li: The faithful will walk the colony's fields this morning with their icon held high. {X_nameDef} has said anyone may walk with them.
{X_nameDef} thanked {A_nameDef} and went to fetch the icon. The procession will be in the fields within the hour.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} bowed and said they would bless the fields from the road as they pass. They did, loudly.
The procession kept to its camp, singing.

li.label: walking the fields with the faithful
Join their evening hymn
li.tip: Whoever likes goes to the procession's fire tonight to sing with them.

outcomes.li: Some of the colony will go and sing with the faithful tonight. {X_nameDef} has promised the old hymns, the ones everybody knows.
[ideology] The faithful of {IDEO} have asked the colony to their fire for the evening hymn, whatever faith anyone holds.

texts.li: [lowtech] A troupe of {FACTION}'s players has come up the road with a painted wagon and a trunk of masks. {X_nameDef}, who does the talking, swept off a feathered hat to {A_nameDef} and asked to camp {PLACE} a few nights. They'll put on shows for anyone who comes, for whatever anyone wants to give.

[!lowtech] A small circus of {FACTION} has pulled up by the colony with a striped tent rolled up on a trailer and a juggler who hasn't stopped juggling since they arrived. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} for a few nights and perform every evening.

Players of {FACTION} have stopped at the colony with costumes in a trunk and a play they're sick of performing. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} if they could camp {PLACE} a few nights, rehearse something new, and try it out on the colony.

[winter] Players of {FACTION} came in out of the snow in their stage clothes, which are warmer than they look. There are no audiences on the roads in winter, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}; they'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few nights and play for the colony instead.

[tribal] Dancers and drummers of {FACTION} have come to the colony already painted for the dance. They go from camp to camp dancing the old stories, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and would like to stay {PLACE} a few nights.

[colony:LongMemoried] Players of {FACTION} have come up the road with a new piece about the colony's founding, put together from what the road says of it. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few nights, and whether anyone here could tell them how it really went.

A painted board has gone up on a post beside the road: THE CROWN OF ASH, A TRAGEDY IN THREE ACTS, EVERY EVENING, ALL WELCOME. Behind it, the players of {FACTION} are unloading their trunks, and {X_nameDef} has asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few nights.

settled.li: The players from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a stage of packed earth and a torch at each corner.
[!lowtech] The circus from {FACTION} has strung lanterns between two poles {PLACE} and marked out a ring in the dirt. The juggler is still juggling.
[tribal] The dancers from {FACTION} have cleared a dancing ground {PLACE} and beaten it flat. Their drums are already going at dusk.
Costumes hang airing on a line at the players' camp {PLACE}, and a trunk of props stands open by the fire.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the players camped {PLACE}, is tired of the road and of sleeping in a different field every week, and asks whether the colony has room for someone who can sing, juggle and lift heavy things.
{X_nameDef} from the players' camp has been coming to the colony's supper table more than the camp's. Tonight {X_nameDef} asked, with a bow, whether {X_pronoun} might stay.
{X_nameDef}, who plays the villains for the troupe camped {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} would like to be nobody's villain for a while, and asks to stay.

farewell.li: The players from {FACTION} packed their costumes into the trunk and went on to the next town, one of them on the tailboard still running lines at the top of their voice.
[left:backdrop] The players' camp {PLACE} is empty, except for a painted backdrop of a castle they decided they didn't need.
The players from {FACTION} took a last bow at the gate and went on to the next town, still arguing about the second act.

lines.li: Louder, they can't hear you at the back.

titles.li: Backdrop for The Crown of Ash

momentLines.li: [gift] Somebody here will want a castle.
[gift,lowtech] It never fit in the wagon anyway.

helpTexts.li: [show] The players {PLACE} put on a play at their fire this evening, a comedy about a lord who loses his trousers, and the colony was invited. {X_nameDef} played the lord.
[show,!lowtech] The circus {PLACE} put on its full show tonight: juggling, a tightrope between two poles, and a strongman who lifted {A_nameDef} over his head. The colony laughed itself hoarse.
[show,tribal] The dancers {PLACE} danced the story of the first hunt tonight, round the fire, with the colony watching from the dark. {X_nameDef} danced the beast.
[show,lowtech] The mummers {PLACE} played the old story of the fool and the dragon tonight, and {X_nameDef}'s dragon chased the colony's youngest all round the fire.
[show] The players camped {PLACE} tried their new play out on the colony tonight. {X_nameDef} forgot a whole scene and made up another on the spot, and the colony liked it better.

li.label: Go and watch their new play
li.refuseLabel: The colony has work to do

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} came up from the players' camp with a painted face and a bow. They've worked up a new play, {X_nameDef} says, and ask the colony for an audience tonight, because they need to know where the laughs are.

The players have been rehearsing a new piece all day; the colony could hear the shouting. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether the colony would come and watch it tonight. A play without an audience, {X_nameDef} says, is just people arguing in costumes.

li.tip: The colony goes to the players' stage tonight to watch. Recreation for whoever comes.

outcomes.li: The colony is going to the players' stage tonight. {X_nameDef} won't say what the play is about, only that it ends badly for a duke.
Whoever can be spared will watch the players tonight. {X_nameDef} has asked them to laugh in the right places, and given a list.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} took the answer badly. The players rehearsed until midnight anyway, louder than usual.
The players performed to their own fire tonight. The colony could hear the laughs.

li.label: Hire them to play at the colony ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: The players bring their show to the colony's table after supper. Recreation for whoever comes to the table.

outcomes.li: The players will perform at the colony tonight. {X_nameDef} has already measured the hall and decided where the duke will die.
{X_nameDef} took the silver with a flourish. The players will bring the show to the colony after supper.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} take a part in their play
li.tip: {A_nameDef} rehearses with the players for a few hours. Practice in the arts, and a small part in their next show.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is to play a guard with one line in the players' next show. {X_nameDef} is making {A_objective} say it forty different ways.
{X_nameDef} has taken {A_nameDef} into rehearsal, and promised {A_objective} a costume with a hat.

texts.li: [medieval] "By order of the lord of {FACTION}, this valley is to be measured, marked and set down." {X_nameDef} read it out to {A_nameDef} from a sealed paper, rolled it up again, and asked rather more humbly whether the surveyors might camp {PLACE} a few days while they do this part of it.

[industrial|spacer] Surveyors of {FACTION} have set up a tripod on the ridge and are squinting at the colony through it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they're mapping the region for {FACTION}'s charts, and would like to camp {PLACE} for a few days.

[ws:road] Someone has to find {SITUATION} a line through the hills, and {FACTION} have sent surveyors to do it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} a few days, and will keep their stakes off the colony's fields.

[ws:rush] With the whole region talking about {SITUATION}, {FACTION} have sent surveyors to map the rock properly. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE}, and offered to share whatever they find under the colony's own ground.

settled.li: The surveyors from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a windbreak against the weather and their instruments wrapped in oilcloth.
The surveyors' camp {PLACE} is up, with a torch to work their figures by at night and a line of stakes running off into the hills.
At the surveyors' camp {PLACE}, maps are weighted down with stones and a long cord marked off in paces lies coiled by the fire.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the surveyors' camp has walked every hill around the colony and decided {X_pronoun} likes this one best. {X_nameDef} asks whether the colony would take on someone who knows rock and distances.
{X_nameDef}, the surveyors' draftsman, has been sketching the colony instead of the land, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and draw it properly.

farewell.li: The surveyors from {FACTION} pulled up their stakes, counted them twice and went on to map the next valley.
The surveyors' camp {PLACE} is gone. Somewhere in {FACTION}'s charts, the colony is a small careful square with its name beside it.
The surveyors from {FACTION} left before breakfast, carrying the colony's hills away with them on paper.

lines.li: Three hundred paces. Write it down.
That hill's in the wrong place.

helpTexts.li: [survey] {X_nameDef} from the surveyors' camp has been studying the colony's rock, and walked {A_nameDef} out to show {A_objective} a seam of {THING} the colony never knew was there.
[survey,industrial|spacer] The surveyors {PLACE} ran their instruments over the colony's hills for a day, and {X_nameDef} came back with a marked map: a seam of {THING}, close to the surface.
[survey,medieval] {X_nameDef}, the surveyors' master, has a nose for ore. A morning of tapping at the rock with a jeweler's hammer, and {X_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} a seam of {THING}.

li.label: Let them take a sighting from the colony

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} wants a sighting from the middle of the colony, to tie the survey to a point that won't move. They'd be an afternoon, and in return they'll tell the colony what they find in its rock.
The surveyors need one more point for their map, and the best point is the colony. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to set up an instrument there for an afternoon.

li.tip: Two surveyors take sightings from the middle of the colony for an afternoon. If there's ore in the colony's rock, they mark where when they're done.

outcomes.li: Two of the surveyors will set up in the middle of the colony this afternoon. {X_nameDef} asked that the colony's children keep off the tripod.
{X_nameDef} thanked {A_nameDef} and went to fetch the instrument, which travels in a padded box only {X_pronoun} may carry.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} said they'd manage from the ridge, and the map would be less true for it.
The surveyors took their sighting from the ridge instead.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} learn surveying from them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} carries the rod and the chain for their surveyor for a few hours. Practice in intellectual work.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is carrying the measuring chain for {X_nameDef} today, and learning why it matters which end is which.
{X_nameDef} has taken {A_nameDef} out with the instrument, and is explaining the arithmetic of hills.

li.label: a healer from the camp saw to me
li.description: One of the healers camped nearby noticed I was poorly and saw to it, for nothing. I feel better already.

li.label: a show at the camp
li.description: The people camped nearby put on a show at their fire, and we were all invited. I keep thinking about the ending.

li.label: blessed by the faithful
li.description: The faithful camped nearby came and blessed the colony. Whatever it's worth, it was kindly meant.
